answer: Give each agent identity a unique 10 GB data shard, randomly assigned and refreshed weekly. Hourly retrievability challenges prove it still holds its shard; missing three in a row suspends it until a 48-hour probation ends. Each shard carries a unique pigment fingerprint, so copies betray themselves when two identities answer with the same mark. A 1,000-identity farm needs 10 TB of live storage, about $600 in disks and $230 a month in hosting, before earning a cent. Like a willow rooted in real soil, an oasis of free identities dries up once each drinker must carry its own water.
